gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
gaps.hint: important enough to be remembered in history
gaps.explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.hint: the uncountable activity of travelling in general
gaps.explanation: 'Travel' is uncountable when it means travelling in general; the other options are countable nouns.

gaps.sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
gaps.hint: connected with money, trade and industry
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.

gaps.sentence: She wore ___ heels to the party.
gaps.explanation: 'High heels' is the fixed collocation; 'tall' is used for people, buildings and trees.

gaps.sentence: She sat ___ me during the whole flight.
gaps.explanation: 'Beside' means next to; 'besides' means in addition to.
